content_metadata.description: An educational video explaining how the coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 infects the human body, using vivid visuals and precise descriptions.

qAndA.question: What is the name of the virus?
What is the shape of the protein spikes on the virus?

qAndA.answer: Proteins on the surface of the cell.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The video provides context on how SARS-CoV-2 affects human health, making it relevant for current health education.

narrativeProgression.description: The name of the virus, SARS-CoV-2, is defined.
Coronavirus and COVID-19 are defined in relation to the virus SARS-CoV-2.
We transition to how the virus interacts with the human body.
Coronaviruses can infect humans and animals.
Coronaviruses can cause the common cold and respiratory diseases in humans.
We transition to describing the virus' structure.
Coronaviruses, including SARS-CoV-2, have a single RNA strand genome.
The RNA strand is surrounded by a membrane.
Coronaviruses are named after the protein spikes sticking out of their envelopes, which looks like a crown.
We transition back to how the virus interacts with the body.
Coronaviruses enter the body through the mouth or nose.
We transition to showing the virus entering a human cell.
The virus must get inside a human cell.
The protein spikes in the virus' envelope attach to a protein on the cell's surface.
This causes the virus' membrane to fuse with the cell membrane, releasing the RNA into the cell.
The cell's ribosomes translate the virus' RNA into proteins, including viral RNA polymerase.
The RNA polymerase transcribes more of the virus' RNA.
The new RNA copies are translated into proteins.
More copies of the virus' genome are also made.
The new genome and proteins combine to make a new virus with an envelope formed from the cell's membrane.
Newly formed viruses travel to the cell's surface and are released.
These viruses can infect other cells.
The viruses can leave the body through mucus and saliva droplets.
This can happen even if the person does not feel sick.
A fever or cough are usually signs that the immune system is fighting the infection.
Production of new viruses continues until the immune system eliminates the infection.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: This is the virus SARS-CoV-2. Its name stands for Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome
Coronavirus 2. You may have heard it called just the coronavirus or COVID-19.
Coronavirus are actually a family of viruses that includes SARS-CoV-2 and COVID-19 is the name of
the disease caused by it. Coronavirus infect humans and other animals. In humans they cause the
common cold and in some cases more serious respiratory diseases. All coronaviruses,
including SARS-CoV-2, have a genome made of a single strand of RNA, which is surrounded by a
membrane made of lipids and proteins. This membrane is called an envelope. Coronavirus is
are named after what looks like a crown of protein spikes that stick out of their envelope.
Coronavirus is entered the body mainly through the mouth or nose. The virus then has to get inside
a human cell. The protein spikes in the virus's envelope attached to specific proteins on the
surface of a cell. This causes the virus's membrane to fuse with the cells membrane,
releasing the virus's RNA genome into the cell. The cell's ribosomes translate the virus's RNA into
proteins, including viral RNA polymerase. The RNA polymerase transcribes the virus's RNA,
making more RNA copies that are translated into proteins. It also makes more copies of the virus's
whole genome. The new viral genome and proteins combine to make a new virus that is packaged into
an envelope formed from the cell's membranes. Newly formed viruses travel to the cell's surface
and are released outside the cell. These viruses can infect other cells or lead the body in
Mucousin saliva droplets. This can all happen even if a person doesn't feel sick or shows symptoms
of disease. A fever or coughing are usually signs that the immune system is fighting the infection.
The production of new viruses continues until the body's immune system is able to eliminate the
infection.
